sections.content: The se-passive is especially good at describing a sustained pattern of exclusion or requirement — something that kept happening, not a single decision by one named authority. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En la práctica, se favorecía sistemáticamente a la 'república de españoles' sobre la 'república de indios'.
items.english: In practice, the 'republic of Spaniards' was systematically favored over the 'republic of Indians'.

items.spanish: Para acceder a la universidad o a un cargo público, se exigía presentar un certificado de 'limpieza de sangre'.
items.english: To gain access to university or a public post, a 'blood purity' certificate had to be presented.

items.spanish: Se reservaban los cargos más altos casi exclusivamente para los peninsulares.
items.english: The highest posts were reserved almost exclusively for those born in Spain.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, se acumuló tanto resentimiento en torno a esta exclusión que buena parte del liderazgo independentista saldría de esas familias.
items.english: Over time, so much resentment built up around this exclusion that much of the independence leadership would come from those very families.

sections.content: Notice the difference in tense between se favorecía / se exigía / se reservaban (imperfect — describing a standing rule or repeated practice) and se generó / se acumuló (preterite — a process that built up and eventually reached a conclusion). The se-passive works with both, and the choice of tense carries real meaning.
